service.description: Create a Task in a Project.

Updates a task. A new rootWorkEffortId moves it to that project with its sub-tasks (the whole subtree takes the new project, design-projects.md §5 "The work item tree"): its parent stays only when it is in the new project (else it becomes a top-level task there; a parentWorkEffortId given with it must be in the new project), and the memberships of the subtree in the old project's milestones, releases, sprints and components end.

return.message: Task ${parentWorkEffortId} is not in project ${rootWorkEffortId}, so ${workEffortId} cannot go under it

service.description: The rest of a task's move to another project (update#Task): the task's sub-tasks at every depth take the new project, the task leaves a parent left in the old project (clearParent), and the memberships of the subtree in plan items of another project end.

Puts a task in a plan item of its project (a milestone, release, sprint or component: WorkEffortAssoc of assocTypeEnumId from the plan item to the task), ending its membership in any other of that kind, as set#TaskMilestone does; an empty planWorkEffortId takes it out of the kind. A plan item of another project is refused.
The task's release (set#TaskPlanItem WeatRelease); empty takes it out of its release.
The task's component (set#TaskPlanItem WeatComponent); empty takes it out of its component.

The task's sprint (set#TaskPlanItem WeatSprint); empty takes it back to the backlog. A sprint that is complete, closed or cancelled takes no items. A change in a sprint in progress is a scope change: the audit log gets a row for the membership (EntityAuditLog of mantle.work.effort.WorkEffortAssoc, pkPrimaryValue the sprint, pkSecondaryValue the task, changedFieldName fromDate when added and thruDate when taken out) with the user who made it, which ProjectReportServices.get#SprintScopeChanges reads.

The rank (sequenceNum) of a task in its project's backlog and sprint lists, which show the project's tasks at every depth in one order: right after previousWorkEffortId, else right before nextWorkEffortId, else first. The ranks are one order over the whole project, so the tree's order of siblings (set#TaskRank) stays the same order: the task takes the middle of the gap it goes into, and when that gap is closed, or a task of the project has no rank yet, every task of the project is numbered again 1000, 2000, … in the order it had. The order is by rank, then (no rank) by the number in the key.

workEffortId depends on (is blocked by) toWorkEffortId, finish to start, with lagDays working days between the end of toWorkEffortId and the start of workEffortId (WorkEffortAssoc WeatDependsOn, whose direction is fixed this way). Refused: an item depending on itself, on one of its ancestors or descendants (a parent's span holds its sub-items), a dependency that closes a loop (toWorkEffortId already depends on workEffortId, at any remove), a negative lag, and a work item or plan item not found. A dependency already there takes the new lag (created false).
Ends the dependency of workEffortId on toWorkEffortId (thruDate now); removed false when there was none.

Moves or resizes a work item, or a milestone, release or sprint, on the timeline: its start (estimatedStartDate) and due (estimatedCompletionDate) as days, yyyy-MM-dd in the user's time zone (a time of day the field had is kept; an empty text clears the date, a parameter not given leaves it). Refused when it would be due before it starts. - shiftDays (a bar dragged along): its own dates move by that many days (startDay and dueDay not given), so an item with only a due date, or a parent with none of its own, moves too. - moveSubtree (a parent's summary bar dragged): its sub-items at every depth move by the same number of days. - autoSchedule: the work items that depend on it (WeatDependsOn, at any remove) and would start before the next business day after their predecessor's due day plus the lag move forward to it, keeping their length in business days; business days as mantle.work.EventServices.get#FutureBusinessDay counts them (Saturday and Sunday, and the holidays of the project's organization, ownerPartyId, skipped). An item is only moved later, never earlier, and an item done (Complete, Closed, Cancelled) is not moved. Each dependent is moved on its own: one that fails is logged and named in failedList, the rest go on. movedList: every item whose dates changed, {workEffortId, startDay, dueDay}.

The status flow of a task: its own statusFlowId, else its project's (rootWorkEffortId), else Default (impl-projects.md F11); the flow's transitions from the task's status (toStatusId and transitionName, by the target's sequence) and the statuses of the flow in sequence order (flowStatusIds).

A task's status along its status flow (get#TaskStatusFlow: its own, else its project's, else Default, with WorkEffortDevelopment's In Review and In Testing): a move the flow has not is refused with the framework's message. Complete takes the resolution given, else Completed, and the actual completion date; Cancelled the resolution given, else Won't Complete; going back to an open status from Complete, Closed or Cancelled clears them. The update#WorkEffort it makes runs the status rules (recurring tasks, the dates).

if.script: // the framework's message for a move its status flows have not (StatusFlowTransitionNotFoundTemplate) const nameOf = (id) => ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.StatusItem').condition('statusId', id).useCache(true).one()?.description || null const localized = ec.l10n.localize('StatusFlowTransitionNotFoundTemplate') const template = localized && localized !== 'StatusFlowTransitionNotFoundTemplate' ? localized : 'Status change not allowed from ${lookedUpStatusName || lookedUpStatusId} to ${parameterStatusName || parameterStatusId}' ec.message.addError(ec.resource.expand(template, '', {fullEntityName: 'Work Effort', lookedUpStatusId: oldStatusId, lookedUpStatusName: nameOf(oldStatusId), parameterStatusId: statusId, parameterStatusName: nameOf(statusId)}))

service.description: Moves a task in its project's work item tree (the view-tree of WorkItems and WorkItemDetail's sub-items): under parentWorkEffortId (empty for the top level) after previousSiblingId (empty for the first), the parameters the tree posts. The parent must be a task of the same project and neither the task nor one of its descendants; the previous sibling must be a child of the new parent. The rank among the new siblings comes from set#TaskRank; a change of parent is in the audit log (WorkEffort.parentWorkEffortId).

The rank (sequenceNum) of a task among its siblings (the tasks of the same parent, or at the top level of its project), right after previousSiblingId (empty for the first). Ranks are in gaps of 1000: the task takes the middle of the gap it goes into, and when the gap is closed, or a sibling has no rank yet, the siblings are numbered again 1000, 2000, … in their order. The order is by rank, then (no rank) by the number in the key.

service.description: The repeat rule of a task (design-projects.md §5 "Recurring work items"): rrule an RFC 5545 RRULE value (FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1), on the task's WorkEffortRecurrence, which makes it the series; recurFromCompletion Y counts the next dates from the day one is completed rather than from its due date. An instance of a series sets the rule of its series. An empty rule stops the repeating (the rule is removed; the items made stay). A task needs a due date (or a start) to repeat.

The next item of a recurring task, when one is completed or cancelled (skipped; to stop instead, the rule is removed first, set#TaskRecurrence): a copy of it (type, name, description, project, parent, assignees and team, watchers, priority, labels, component, estimate and visibility; not its sprint, time, comments or files), In Planning, due on the next date of its series' rule, counted from the series' due date (the date after this item's due) or, with recurFromCompletion, from the day it was completed; a start keeps its distance before the due date. The new item is linked from the series by WeatRecurrenceInstance with its due date. Nothing is made past the rule's end, for a task not in a series, or when the next one was made already. Run by the WorkEffort status rule (Work.secas.xml) on Complete and Cancelled.

Run by the WorkEffortParty rule of WorkEffort.secas.xml; a failure is logged, not the assignment's.
